rows.Risk Statement: Risk of a cyber incident that causes a major disruption to business operations. IT resilience risks materialise – including the capability to recover systems following an outage
rows.Action Detail:
• Continued intelligence gathering from attacks on other companies including the impact of AI. 
• Ongoing programme of cyber resilience improvements, informed by NIST framework maturity assessment, focussing on technical controls and governance via the Cyber Governance and Risk Management Forum. 
• IT Disaster Recovery (DR) Acceleration Programme supplemented by cSET Assessment Improvement Initiative to enhance prioritisation. 
• Exercise CARBON 
• Audit Committee Update (October)
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Risk remains elevated, persistent and evolving. 
• Threat intelligence and increasingly capable AI adversaries are challenging existing system interdependencies, recovery sequencing, third-party exposures and the use of unsupported tools. 
• Audit Committee agenda includes an update from the CISO on the Cyber Transformation Programme, informed by a maturity assessment, including reducing vulnerabilities, strengthening infrastructure and governance enhancements. 
• IT Disaster Recovery (DR) Acceleration Programme supplemented by cSET Assessment Improvement Initiative to enhance prioritisation. 
• Exercise Carbon, which simulates the escalation of a cyber incident and associated business impacts to the SET and Board is in progress.
rows.KAR Mitigation List:
• Strategic projects focused on the visibility of technology assets, reduction in vulnerabilities, threat detection and response capability.
• Governance in place aligned to refreshed strategy via the Cyber Governance & Risk Forum and the Cyber Regulatory SteerCo, to drive and monitor strategic execution and compliance across the complex regulatory landscape.
• IT Disaster Recovery Acceleration Programme transitioning from assessing test and restore capacity for individual applications to addressing the complexities of sequenced restoration of multiple applications following an incident.
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure in Information technology or cyber security

rows.SET Risk Owner: SVP Chief Digital, Data & AI Officer; EVP Operations & IT
rows.Risk Statement: Failures in data loss prevention and / or infornation governance
rows.Action Detail:
• Progress with governance and monitoring enhancements. 
• Remediation of high-risk areas including technical restrictions on the use of unapproved AI and 3rd party sharing technologies.  
• Ongoing delivery of Data Loss Prevention projects including targeted control framework roll-out
• Audit Committee Update (October)
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Data Enablement Council (DEC) maturing, driving greater focus on the management, protection and utilisation of unique data assets, strengthening governance and informing risk based decisions. 
• Remediation of high-risk areas including technical restrictions on the use of unapproved AI and 3rd party sharing technologies. 
• Data Loss Prevention enhancements underway, including implementation of a strengthened control framework. 
Roll out of agentic AI tools with enhanced training focused on data protection. 
• EU formally adopted amendments in the Digital Omnibus package, delaying key compliance deadlines for high-risk Artificial Intelligence systems to December 2027.
rows.KAR Mitigation List:
• Data Enablement Council (incorporating AI governance) in place and maturing to drive regulatory compliance and to monitor risk based decisions, governance of data and information protection.
• Project Streamline continuing with an “AI first” approach to AI governance to accelerate and simplify compliance across multiple regulatory domains, including data privacy.
• Closure of remaining actions from GIA EU AI Act report linked to evolving EU regulations.
• Data security and information governance enhancements including strengthened control frameworks.
• Technical remediation of high-risk areas including restrictions on the use of unapproved AI or third party sharing platforms.
• Contractual terms and conditions with AI and IT vendors prohibit the use of AZ data for training third party models.
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure to collect and manage data in line with legal and regulatory requirements; Failure in Information technology or cyber security

rows.Risk Statement: Risks of tariffs and other government policies that impact pricing and / or access to medicines across various markets
rows.Action Detail:
• Implementation of MFN pricing regime and provision of assured data to US government.   
• Monitoring of US government approach to orphan drug designation.
• Board oversight of strategy and execution as part of MTP/LTP reviews.
• Ongoing regulatory monitoring across functions.
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Intensifying global focus on drug pricing, affordability and market access. 
• Inflation Reduction Act implementation and MFN impacts incorporated into LTP, MTP, pricing controls and market strategies, including assessment of launch implications in MFN basket markets. 
• Audit-ready MFN data provided to US government.
• U.S. Trade Representative’s investigation into pricing of innovative medicines in Germany and the impact of exporter products within the EU and UK; issued primarily on Chinese patient data disclosure of the convergence of pricing/access risks with geopolitics.
rows.KAR Mitigation List:
• Pricing and launch strategy impacts incorporated into latest forecasts and assessed during MTP/LTP
• Preparation of pricing information for MFN reference countries, with auditable support
• Continued government advocacy focused on pricing for innovative medicines, alongside broader policy matters
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Pricing, affordability, access and competitive pressures; Failures or delays in the quality and execution of the Group's commercial strategies; Failure or delay in the delivery of our pipeline or launch of new medicines; Geopolitical and / or macroeconomic volatility disrupts operation of our global business; Failure to achieve strategic plans or meet targets or expectations

rows.Key Active Risk: Harnessing the Power of AI, Strategic Execution and Pipeline Delivery
rows.SET Risk Owner: CEO, SET, SVP Chief Digital, Data & AI Officer
rows.Risk Statement: Failure to fully execute key elements of the company’s strategy – including pipeline execution risk (e.g. new modalities), implementation of major transformation programmes and the failure to adopt and scale AI utilising unique data assets
rows.Action Detail:
• Risk management resources embedded in pipeline and technology transformation programmes. 
• Responsible delivery of priority AI programmes.
• Key technology programmes including implementation of lessons learned from initial • Axial deployments and the Customer 2030 programme. 
• Audit Committee Deep Dive (December)
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Catalyst rich period continues with multiple clinical read‑outs, alongside preparation for upcoming product launches
• New modalities introduce requirements for novel materials and new manufacturing processes, with a focus on sustained supply
• Multiple enterprise scale transformations (e.g. Transforming Care, Axial, CRM and major Capex programmes) continue, each with a range of execution risks being actively monitored and managed
• Lessons learned from Axial deployment in Mexico being collated and fed into future plans
rows.KAR Mitigation List:
• Existing enterprise-level Pipeline to Product Governance
• Close monitoring and SET sponsorship is in place for all enterprise-scale transformation and capital programmes, with embedded risk surveillance
• Operations, procurement, supply chain and capital workstreams aligning to the requirements of new modalities
• Delivery governance in place in Enterprise AI to track delivery of “must win” AI30 projects across functions.
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure or delay in the delivery of our pipeline or launch of new medicines; Geopolitical and / or macroeconomic volatility disrupts operation of our global business; Failure to achieve strategic plans or meet targets or expectations

rows.Risk Statement: Failure to meet commercial demand both now and in the future and maintain supply of compliant, quality medicines
rows.Action Detail:
• Progress in delivery of capital programmes supporting growth and new modalities.  
• Monitoring of availability of critical construction inputs that could be impacted by ‘chokepoints’ 
• Embedded risk management in capital projects.  
• N-tier mapping and self healing supply chain projects providing incremental supply chain visibility and flexibility.
• Audit Committee Deep Dive (October)
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Continued complexity in new capacity investment decisions given growth objectives, regional manufacturing needs and modality-specific requirements.
• Supply chain activity managed with increased emphasis on deeper-tier supplier visibility, self healing capabilities, scenario analysis and resilient sourcing.
• N-tier mapping programme advancing to enhance visibility beyond Tier 1 suppliers as a strategic enabler for resilience and compliance with funding for AI First, EAI developed prototype agreed.
rows.KAR Mitigation List:
• Supply chain mapping and Supply Chain Resilience programmes continuing to enable proactive horizon scanning, scenario planning and a more agile response to disruptions.
• N-Tier mapping programme progressing, including business case finalisation.
• Monitoring of availability of critical inputs that may be impacted by potential ‘chokepoints’ in global trade.
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure to maintain supply of compliant, quality medicines

rows.Key Active Risk: Rapid Evolution of Regulation, Regulatory Fragmentation and Increased Scrutiny
rows.Risk Statement: Risks relating to complex, fast moving, conflicting and fragmented regulations impacting on the ability of global businesses to operate at scale
rows.Action Detail:
• Readiness for compliance with new regulations across various domains. 
• Changes in regulatory landscape notably in relation to AI and data.
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Regulatory complexity persists, impacting globalised operating models and increasing compliance risk and operational complexity. 
• Key areas include cyber, data, commercial, environmental, use of animals in research and employment domains, with cross-border implications requiring coordinated responses. 
• New supply chain security laws in China being assessed, with support from third parties, but could potentially conflict with laws in other jurisdictions and existing global processes. 
• Proposed amendments to US COINS Act could potentially prohibit U.S. investments, joint ventures and licensing deals in Chinese biotech and pharmaceutical industries.
rows.KAR Mitigation List:
• Regulatory compliance programmes continue across multiple teams (e.g. NIS2, U.S. and China data transfer regulations, EU Pay Transparency, Trade Sanctions)
• Project Streamline continuing with an “AI first” approach to AI governance, accelerating and simplifying compliance across multiple regulatory domains
• Ongoing advocacy to reinforce the importance of PFAS derogations
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure to collect and manage data in line with legal and regulatory requirements

rows.Risk Statement: Risks relating to geopolitical tensions and operating in conflict zones including trade sanctions
rows.Quarterly Update:
• Continued monitoring of the situation in the Middle East and Ukraine with continued focus on employee safety and maintaining supply of medicines to patients. 
• Regional and local Incident Management Teams and Business Continuity Plans on standby should they be required to be reactivated. 
• Developments in Russia in light of recent confiscation of other multi-national company assets with warehousing location being actively reviewed to ensure supply of medicine is not disrupted.
rows.KAR Mitigation List: • Ongoing monitoring of the global environment and targeted reviews of existing Business Continuity Plans.
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure to achieve strategic plans or meet targets or expectations

rows.Risk Statement: Risks relating to patents protection,  government investigations and commercial litigation
rows.Quarterly Update: • Continued legal response to enforce our patents and defend litigation matters.
rows.KAR Mitigation List: • Continued robust defence of patents and other legal matters across multiple jurisdictions.
rows.Linked Principal Risks: Failure to meet regulatory & ethical expectations on commercial practices, including anti-bribery and corruption, and scientific exchanges; Failure to obtain, defend and enforce effective IP protection or IP challenges by 3rd parties; Adverse outcome of litigation and / or governmental investigations
